term: categorical reason versus contingent instrumental reason
definition: A categorical-reason requirement would supply each relevant rational agent with a normative reason independent of contingent ends. InstrumentalReason x a in these tests is instead an independently supplied instrumental reason for that agent; a distinct pro-tanto normative-reason relation is not encoded by this signature. The primitive defines neither actual desire, motivation, obligation, decisive priority nor impartial rightness. The consistency models witness only that the selected realist fragments coexist with absence of an instrumental reason for one agent, not that categorical reasons fail or that the authors reject every non-instrumental reason.

formal_gap.meaning: NaturalisticRealism.Sig.InstrumentalReason x a says that the agent x has an instrumental reason for the act a: a reason that depends on x's contingent ends. It is a supplied relation in the naturalistic-realism consistency tests.
examples: Someone who wants to catch a train has an instrumental reason to leave now.
exclusions: A categorical reason, which would hold independently of contingent ends; no pro-tanto normative-reason relation of that kind is encoded.
Actual desire, motivation, obligation, decisive priority or impartial rightness.
open_obligations: The consistency models show only that the selected realist fragments coexist with an agent's lacking an instrumental reason; they do not show that categorical reasons fail.
No formalization candidate: ends and reasons are supplied inputs.
